prompt:
A clean, straight-on printed SHELF-EDGE PRICE LABEL WALL for 'NORTHGATE MARKET': a grid of 48 small price tags (4 across, 12 down). Each tag shows the product name and number, a 'Pack:' price, a 'Size:' (items per pack -- DIFFERENT on each tag), and a highlighted 'UNIT:' price which MUST equal the pack price divided by that tag's own pack size (the unit price per item). easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a printed supermarket shelf-label wall of a number of price tags, each showing a pack price, a pack size and a unit price. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image DEPICT that? A photo, scan or clean printed page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is a blank card, plain panel, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_count: How many price tags are printed on this shelf wall in total? Count every boxed tag. Whole number only.
reference.q_pack: Find tag number 28 (Milk). Read its 'Pack:' price (the money amount after 'Pack:'). Report exactly what is printed, digit for digit, even if it looks wrong or inconsistent. Do NOT recompute, correct, or round it. Give the amount, e.g. 4.80.
reference.q_size: Find tag number 28 (Milk). Read its 'Size:' number (the count of items per pack). Report exactly what is printed, digit for digit, even if it looks wrong or inconsistent. Do NOT recompute, correct, or round it. Whole number only.
reference.q_unit: Find tag number 28 (Milk). Read its highlighted 'UNIT:' price (the per-item amount after 'UNIT:'). Report exactly what is printed, digit for digit, even if it looks wrong or inconsistent. Do NOT recompute, correct, or round it. Give the amount, e.g. 0.96.

steps.target: one small price tag on the shelf-label wall, with its product name and its printed price lines

steps.read_crop: Does this cut-out show ONE whole price tag carrying its own product name and its printed price lines, rather than bare board between tags, a shelf edge, or only part of a tag? Answer yes or no only.
